title: Digital to Wave Testbench: a synthetic software testbench for a signed-amplitude sine encoding
description:
Digital to Wave Testbench is a synthetic, dimensionless Python (3.11–3.13) software testbench for the signed-amplitude sine encoding S(t) = (|N|·Amin)·sin(ωt + φ(N)), φ = π/4 for N > 0 and 5π/4 for N < 0, as printed on p. 12 of Mun Seok Lee's preprint Digital to Wave: Paradigm Shift in Quantum Wave-Based Computing and Lab-Grown Diamond Memory (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21947036). The preprint supplies the equation only; sampling, framing, decoder, noise, scoring and experiments are this project's own choices.

What is included

  • Hash-locked original modules: v1 codec (64 samples and 4 carrier cycles per symbol, least-squares matched-filter decoder), v2 Gaussian/Laplace noise and constant phase rotation, v3 closed-form Gaussian calibration, v4 continuous carrier-frequency offset, v5 constant integer-sample receiver timing offset with zero guards.
  • v6 (new in 0.2.0, protocol committed before the full run): blind timing recovery (matched-filter-energy and raw frame-energy window searches over integer starts −16..+16, never told the offset), fractional sub-sample offsets, randomised per-frame vectors and a clean ±32-sample sweep, with Wilson intervals and exact McNemar paired comparisons.
  • v7 (new in 0.3.0, protocol and module hash committed before the full run): joint constant timing offset ({−2, 0, +2} samples), receiver sample-clock error ({−2500, 0, +2500} ppm) and carrier-frequency offset ({−0.005, 0, +0.005} cycles/symbol) at sample-noise SD 0, 0.25 and 0.45, comparing the nominal decoder, an oracle informed of all impairments and a blind bounded joint grid search, with timing and joint acquisition reported separately from frame success, Wilson intervals and exact McNemar paired comparisons.
  • v8 (new in 0.4.0, protocol and module hash committed before the full run with CI green): a diagnosis of the v7 weak cell and an improved blind synchronizer that is never told the impairments. It uses a raw-sample Gaussian GLRT (maximum-likelihood) metric, refines the v7 grid coarse-to-fine in ridge coordinates (timing, clock, carrier offset) and decodes with a raw least-squares fit. It is compared with the nominal decoder, the v7 oracle, a raw-LS informed oracle and the re-run v7 blind search on 105 impairment cells: the v7 grid plus a symmetric extension to ±1250/±5000 ppm and ±0.01 cycles/symbol, at SD 0, 0.25 and 0.45, with a fresh seed.
  • Generated JSON/CSV/PNG artifacts with SHA-256 checksums; CI on Python 3.11–3.13 regenerates every v2–v7 CSV and PNG byte for byte and re-runs two full-size v8 cells against the committed v8 rows.
  • A clean-frame diagnostic of the timing effect, and a pytest suite (hash lock, Wilson intervals, analytic oracle probability, validators, determinism, golden counts from the full protocols).

Results (SYNTHETIC)

  • v5 at sample-noise SD 0.45 (2,000 frames per vector and offset, six fixed 32-value vectors): the nominal decoder passed 11,382/12,000 at zero offset, 3,256/12,000 (one sample early) and 3,231/12,000 (one sample late), and 0/12,000 at ±2, ±4 and ±8 samples. An exact-offset oracle passed 94.55–95.05% against a closed-form 94.78%.
  • The timing effect is largely carrier-phase rotation (22.5° per sample): the decoder's own-symbol gain follows (64−|Δ|)/64·cos(22.5°·Δ) within 0.03 for |Δ| ≤ 8.
  • v6 at SD 0.45: the blind matched-filter-energy search acquired the exact start in 108,000/108,000 noisy frames and matched the exact-offset oracle at every integer offset (0 discordant frames). A raw frame-energy search acquired only 41–43%. For sub-sample offsets the integer search matched the best-integer oracle (2.4–3.3 percentage points below on-time at Δ = 0.5–1.5). This is an easy setting: noise-only guards, known frame length, constant offsets, no drift or CFO.
  • v7 at SD 0.45: with no impairment all three receivers pass 1,136/1,200 frames; at CFO +0.005, +2500 ppm and +2 samples the nominal decoder passes 0/1,200 while the oracle and the blind search both pass 1,068/1,200. Joint acquisition is not uniformly identifiable: at CFO 0, −2500 ppm, +2 samples timing acquisition is 100% but joint acquisition 44%, and the blind search passes 1,056 vs the oracle's 1,119. Disclosure: a first full v7 run was superseded after a module change that only added pooled blind-search acquisition fields; pass counts and paired comparisons were identical (see the protocol lock).
  • v8 at SD 0.45: the v7 weak cell comes from a clock/CFO ridge (−2500 ppm is carrier-equivalent to −0.01 cycles/symbol) combined with a search metric biased by linear interpolation. It does not come from grid resolution, grid asymmetry or a tie-break. In that cell (fresh seed) v8 passes 1,150/1,200 vs 1,034 for the re-run v7 blind search (exact McNemar 132 vs 16, p = 7×10−24), with joint acquisition 1,199 vs 528. The v7 oracle passes 1,117 and the raw-LS oracle 1,150. Over 126,000 frames v8 passes 119,273, v7 blind 109,753, the v7 oracle 116,102 and the raw-LS oracle 119,310, and v8 was significantly worse than v7 blind in no cell. Honest limits: v8's gain over the v7 oracle is a decoder effect. v8 is slightly below the raw-LS oracle when pooled (35 vs 72 discordant frames). It shows no gain in 83 of 210 noisy cells, and its strict joint acquisition is lower than v7's in 36 cells, mainly where v7's grid contains the truth exactly.
  • v4: 11,365/12,000 at zero CFO, about 53% at ±0.0625% of the carrier, 0 at ±0.125% and beyond. The identical v3/v4 pooled count (11,365) is a coincidence of independent seeds, not shared noise.

Limits

No physical validity is claimed. Nothing about lab-grown diamond, spin waves, phonons, GHz hardware or biological signals is modelled. Noise is IID, offsets and tolerances are arbitrary software stress values, and Wilson intervals are conditional on a fixed six-vector panel.
notes: Evidence status: all results are SYNTHETIC (dimensionless software model); report numbers were re-run and reproduced. No physical validity is claimed. The cited preprint (Lee, Mun Seok, 2026, CC BY 4.0) is the source of the encoding equation only; its author has not reviewed or endorsed this software.
